mukta-m0-p100-v2476.quick_english: May the Crusher protect always; may the Crusher guard forever.

mukta-m0-p100-v2477.quick_english: May the Crusher protect always; may the Crusher guard forever.

mukta-m0-p100-v2478.quick_english: May the Radiant One protect, O Great Goddess; may the Golden One guard always.

mukta-m0-p100-v2479.quick_english: May the Radiant One protect; may Great Illusion and Illusion always protect me.

mukta-m0-p100-v2480.quick_english: May the Delightful One protect always; may the Very Radiant One guard at all times.

mukta-m0-p100-v2481.quick_english: May the powers protect always; may they always protect my seal.

mukta-m0-p100-v2482.quick_english: May the yoginīs protect always; may the sky-movers guard at all times.

mukta-m0-p100-v2483.quick_english: May the goddess, the Crusher of the Buffalo, protect everywhere and always.

mukta-m0-p100-v2484.quick_english: Wherever one is, it must not be spoken; it must be carefully concealed.

mukta-m0-p100-v2485.quick_english: Knowledge is easily found everywhere, but this great armor is hard to obtain.

mukta-m0-p100-v2486.quick_english: One should not show the divine hymn or the armor, which is hard for even the gods to obtain.

mukta-m0-p100-v2487.quick_english: O Great Goddess, if it is given to them, one's powers perish gradually.

mukta-m0-p100-v2488.quick_english: And inauspiciousness may come to him; therefore one should conceal it with effort.

mukta-m0-p100-v2489.quick_english: Having written it during an auspicious conjunction, and likewise in Brahma-Indra and in Vaidhṛti...

mukta-m0-p100-v2490.quick_english: In Vaṇija, in Śravaṇā, and in Revatī or in Punarvasu...

mukta-m0-p100-v2491.quick_english: In Aśvinī or in Rohiṇī, or on the third or ninth lunar day...

mukta-m0-p100-v2492.quick_english: On the new moon or on the full moon, at night, and likewise in a secluded place...

mukta-m0-p100-v2493.quick_english: By a guru or by Vaiṣṇavas, and likewise with self-born flowers...

mukta-m0-p100-v2494.quick_english: Then one should wear the armor, a great protection that grants all desires.

mukta-m0-p100-v2495.quick_english: Seeing him, an opponent becomes mute, and a king becomes like a servant.

mukta-m0-p100-v2496.quick_english: In six months or in three months, one certainly becomes a sky-mover.

mukta-m0-p100-v2497.quick_english: One becomes disease-free and strong, and even a king may become a servant.

mukta-m0-p100-v2498.quick_english: The wise one who acts thus is indeed the auspicious Sadāśiva.

mukta-m0-p100-v2499.quick_english: As you are immovable, O Kṛṣṇā, so be steady in me.

mukta-m0-p100-v2500.quick_english: Padmā, the lotus-abiding goddess, is prosperity itself, supremely exalted and holding the auspicious lotus.

mukta-m0-p101-v2501.quick_english: May steady fortune be his, together with his son, wife, and others.

mukta-m0-p101-v2502.quick_english: By whose mere knowledge one may become Sadāśiva himself.

mukta-m0-p101-v2503.quick_english: He may become the son of Pārvatī, honored by all the scriptures.

mukta-m0-p101-v2504.quick_english: Kamalā, beloved of Viṣṇu, should always be served by those who seek knowledge.

mukta-m0-p101-v2505.quick_english: May hrīṃ and Śāṅkarī protect the space between the eyes and the pair of eyes.

mukta-m0-p101-v2506.quick_english: At the base of the lips, in the row of teeth, at the root of the palate, and again in the jaw.

mukta-m0-p101-v2507.quick_english: In the region of the back, likewise in the secret part, and on the left and right sides as well.

mukta-m0-p101-v2508.quick_english: In the knee circle, in the pair of feet, and at the base of the ankles and toes.

mukta-m0-p101-v2509.quick_english: May Kāmeśī, the exalted great goddess, protect every limb.

mukta-m0-p101-v2510.quick_english: May the seer protect; O goddess, beloved of Śambhu, may you always protect everywhere.

mukta-m0-p101-v2511.quick_english: May Ramā, the great goddess, protect; may Māyā, self-ruling by herself, protect.

mukta-m0-p101-v2512.quick_english: May Vijayā protect in the house; may Jayā always protect me.

mukta-m0-p101-v2513.quick_english: May Bhairavī protect everywhere; may Bheruṇḍā always protect.

mukta-m0-p101-v2514.quick_english: May Kālikā always protect me; may Kālarātri always protect.

mukta-m0-p101-v2515.quick_english: May the Yoginīs always protect; may the Mudrās always protect me.

mukta-m0-p101-v2516.quick_english: Everywhere, in all tasks, in all actions, and always.

mukta-m0-p101-v2517.quick_english: Thus this divine armor has been told to you for the accomplishment of all powers.

mukta-m0-p101-v2518.quick_english: O great goddess, not to the deceitful, not to one devoid of devotion, and not to a slanderer.

mukta-m0-p101-v2519.quick_english: One should not show this divine hymn; from showing it, there may be loss of Śiva's grace.

mukta-m0-p101-v2520.quick_english: One should give this supreme armor to a pure Vaiṣṇava.

mukta-m0-p101-v2521.quick_english: One should give the armor; thus it is said, in agreement with all the tantras.

mukta-m0-p101-v2522.quick_english: One should write the mantra with lac, endowed with all the circles.

mukta-m0-p101-v2523.quick_english: With one's own fluids and others' fluids, and endowed with various fragrances.

mukta-m0-p101-v2524.quick_english: On a good lunar day, on an auspicious conjunction, or in Śravaṇā on a Sunday.

mukta-m0-p101-v2525.quick_english: Or when Pūrvabhādrapadā is in conjunction, or in Svātī, on a Tuesday.

mukta-m0-p105-v2601.quick_english: I worship Rama every day, together with Sita and Lakshmana.

mukta-m0-p105-v2602.quick_english: For him the directions are filled with Shiva, and the powers become his maidservants.

mukta-m0-p105-v2603.quick_english: Whoever recites this daily will become devoted to Rama.

mukta-m0-p105-v2604.quick_english: There is no higher secret than this in the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p105-v2605.quick_english: Then, seated to eat, Shankara spoke to Parvati.

mukta-m0-p105-v2606.quick_english: Then I shall eat, O god; let it be eaten by you, O lord.

mukta-m0-p105-v2607.quick_english: You are blessed, you are meritorious, and you are a devotee of Vishnu, O Parvati.

mukta-m0-p105-v2608.quick_english: O Parvati, as I hear the names beginning with the syllable ra.

mukta-m0-p105-v2609.quick_english: Thus, by the word Rama, the supreme Brahman is designated.

mukta-m0-p105-v2610.quick_english: Having said 'Rama,' O great goddess, eat together with me now.

mukta-m0-p105-v2611.quick_english: Then, having eaten, the great goddess remained together with her husband.

mukta-m0-p105-v2612.quick_english: Let it be told to me, O lord; in that I have supreme delight.

mukta-m0-p105-v2613.quick_english: The names of auspicious Rama are more than a thousand.

mukta-m0-p105-v2614.quick_english: Each single name of Vishnu bears fruit surpassing all the Vedas.

mukta-m0-p105-v2615.quick_english: Therefore, merit multiplied a crore times is obtained by the name of Rama alone.

mukta-m0-p105-v2616.quick_english: Lotus-eyed, glorious, lord of kings, chief of the Raghu dynasty.

mukta-m0-p105-v2617.quick_english: Dear to Vishvamitra, self-controlled, devoted to protecting those who seek refuge.

mukta-m0-p105-v2618.quick_english: Vowed to truth, the fruit of vows, always the shelter of Hanuman.

mukta-m0-p105-v2619.quick_english: Protector of Vibhishana, remover of the heads of the ten-necked one.

mukta-m0-p105-v2620.quick_english: The fire to the great pride of Parashurama, the slayer of Tadaka.

mukta-m0-p105-v2621.quick_english: Slayer of Dushana and Trishiras, three-formed, the three qualities, and the three Vedas.

mukta-m0-p105-v2622.quick_english: Protector of the three worlds, bowman, maker of merit in the Dandaka forest.

mukta-m0-p105-v2623.quick_english: Protector in the matter of Jayanta, giver of boons, served by the son of Sumitra.

mukta-m0-p105-v2624.quick_english: Slayer of the illusory Maricha, possessed of great lordship, and mighty-armed.

mukta-m0-p105-v2625.quick_english: He is a great yogi and greatly noble, the giver of the desired kingdom to Sugrīva.

mukta-m0-p109-v2701.quick_english: It is visualized as a dense, cloud-like mass, like the essence of pearls, released in both broken and unbroken streams.

mukta-m0-p109-v2702.quick_english: He is constantly beheld by herds of cows along with their calves looking up.

mukta-m0-p109-v2703.quick_english: He is adorned by cowherds with sticks and nooses raised in their hands.

mukta-m0-p109-v2704.quick_english: The supreme of the supreme is praised with speech that is affectionate and very tender.

mukta-m0-p109-v2705.quick_english: Satisfied with him at the three daily junctures, he grants the desired boon.

mukta-m0-p109-v2706.quick_english: He certainly obtains unshakable prosperity and becomes eloquent.

mukta-m0-p109-v2707.quick_english: O lord, out of compassion please tell the teaching named Trailokyamaṅgala, auspicious for the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p109-v2708.quick_english: It was formerly told out of compassion by Nārāyaṇa to Brahmā.

mukta-m0-p109-v2709.quick_english: It is the most secret truth, embodied as a multitude of Brahman-mantras.

mukta-m0-p109-v2710.quick_english: Having held it and through its recitation, Mahālakṣmī protects the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p109-v2711.quick_english: Durgā, the mother of the three worlds, overcomes Mahiṣa and other great demons.

mukta-m0-p109-v2712.quick_english: Thus Indra and all the other gods may obtain complete sovereignty.

mukta-m0-p109-v2713.quick_english: One should reveal it to a disciple who is endowed with devotion and is a practitioner.

mukta-m0-p109-v2714.quick_english: Prajāpati is the seer of this Trailokyamaṅgala armor.

mukta-m0-p109-v2715.quick_english: Its application is declared for dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation.

mukta-m0-p109-v2716.quick_english: May the eight-syllabled mantra, giver of enjoyment and liberation, protect my forehead and pair of eyes.

mukta-m0-p109-v2717.quick_english: May 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya' always protect my nose, and 'govindāya' protect my tongue.

mukta-m0-p109-v2718.quick_english: May the eighteen-syllabled great mantra and the ten-syllabled mantra protect my throat.

mukta-m0-p109-v2719.quick_english: O Lady of the worlds, may my heart, my two hands, and my breasts be protected by 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya'.

mukta-m0-p109-v2720.quick_english: May the best of mantras, 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya', always protect my pair of sides.

mukta-m0-p109-v2721.quick_english: May the eight-syllabled mantra protect my navel, and may the two-syllabled 'kṛṣṇa' protect it.

mukta-m0-p109-v2722.quick_english: May 'śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ' together with the Kṛṣṇa-ṭha pair always protect my thighs.

mukta-m0-p109-v2723.quick_english: Then, after 'śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ', comes the word 'gopījanavallabha'.

mukta-m0-p109-v2724.quick_english: And may 'hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ' and the ten-syllabled mantra always protect my knees.

mukta-m0-p109-v2725.quick_english: This mantra is eighteen-syllabled; when preceded by hrīṃ and śrīṃ, it becomes twenty-syllabled.

mukta-m0-p120-v2976.quick_english: It should be given to a devoted disciple who is dearer even than one's own life-breaths.

mukta-m0-p120-v2977.quick_english: The sage is Ṛṣi, the meter is Virāṭ, and the deity is Chinnamastakā.

mukta-m0-p120-v2978.quick_english: May the hūṃ syllable protect my head, and may Chinnamastā, radiant with strength, protect it.

mukta-m0-p120-v2979.quick_english: May śrīṃ, hrīṃ, hūṃ, and aiṃ protect my two eyes, and may she who holds three severed heads also protect them.

mukta-m0-p120-v2980.quick_english: The mantra beginning with dhruva is: vajravairocanīye huṃ phaṭ svāhā.

mukta-m0-p120-v2981.quick_english: With the seed syllables śrīṃ, māyā, kūrca, and vāk, followed by vajravairocanīye and hūṃ.

mukta-m0-p120-v2982.quick_english: At her own sides, joyfully causing the stream of blood to be drunk.

mukta-m0-p120-v2983.quick_english: Holding a severed head and scissors, red in color, she grants the desires of the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p120-v2984.quick_english: May the formula beginning with ramā protect the tongue, and may the formula beginning with lajjā protect the throat.

mukta-m0-p120-v2985.quick_english: May the mantra enclosed by ramā protect the two sides, and may Sureśvarī protect them.

mukta-m0-p120-v2986.quick_english: May the goddess enclosed by kūrca always protect the back region.

mukta-m0-p120-v2987.quick_english: Īśvarī, with the seed syllables kūrca and vāk, vajravairocanīye, hūṃ.

mukta-m0-p120-v2988.quick_english: May Chinnamastā, together with her śakti, always protect the pair of thighs.

mukta-m0-p120-v2989.quick_english: May the eternal one who abides in all mantras always protect all my limbs.

mukta-m0-p120-v2990.quick_english: May Ḍākinī protect me on the right, and may Śrī Mahābhairavī protect me.

mukta-m0-p120-v2991.quick_english: May Indrākṣī protect in the northwest, and may Asitāṅgī protect in the north.

mukta-m0-p120-v2992.quick_english: Thus may these eight śaktis, bearing scissors, protect in the directions and intermediate directions.

mukta-m0-p120-v2993.quick_english: Hrīṃ, hrīṃ, may she protect me on the right; O Kālikā on the right, may you protect me.

mukta-m0-p120-v2994.quick_english: Hūṃ, hūṃ, may she protect in the northwest; svāhā, may she always protect in the north.

mukta-m0-p120-v2995.quick_english: Tāra, māyā, vadhū, kūrca, and the phaṭ syllable—this is the great mantra.

mukta-m0-p120-v2996.quick_english: Tārā, accompanied in the sky, is then Mahānīla Sarasvatī.

mukta-m0-p120-v2997.quick_english: By holding and reciting this, one is remembered as the terrible Bhairava named Krodha.

mukta-m0-p120-v2998.quick_english: By whose command Madhumatī goes to the vicinity of the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p120-v2999.quick_english: By the grace of that armor, they receive his command.

mukta-m0-p120-v3000.quick_english: Having worshipped the goddess with fragrance and other offerings, one should recite once using only the root-mantra.

mukta-m0-p124-v3076.quick_english: May the syllable hūṃ, bearing the form of Bhavānī's power, protect me in the heart.

mukta-m0-p124-v3077.quick_english: May Kharvā, the fear-removing goddess-lord, protect me on both cheeks.

mukta-m0-p124-v3078.quick_english: May the goddess covered with a tiger skin, beloved of Śiva, protect me on the hip.

mukta-m0-p124-v3079.quick_english: And may the goddess with red, round eyes always protect me in the hip region.

mukta-m0-p124-v3080.quick_english: May the terrible-mouthed goddess, beloved of Hara, always protect me on the generative organ.

mukta-m0-p124-v3081.quick_english: May the great goddess Maheśvarī, holding a corpse-skull, protect me on the knee-wheel.

mukta-m0-p124-v3082.quick_english: Then may the goddess wearing snake earrings protect me on both feet.

mukta-m0-p124-v3083.quick_english: May the goddess wearing snake-bone ornaments protect me in the border region.

mukta-m0-p124-v3084.quick_english: May the great goddess holding a sword always protect me in the ear.

mukta-m0-p124-v3085.quick_english: May the goddess holding scissors always protect me in disputes among enemies.

mukta-m0-p124-v3086.quick_english: May the goddess wearing snake bracelets always protect me while eating.

mukta-m0-p124-v3087.quick_english: May the goddess seated in the hero posture always protect me during sleep.

mukta-m0-p124-v3088.quick_english: May the goddess whose hip is girdled with a snake protect me in all actions.

mukta-m0-p124-v3089.quick_english: May the goddess situated in the middle of a pyre always protect me in acts of killing.

mukta-m0-p124-v3090.quick_english: May the ornamented goddess, beloved of Hara, protect me.

mukta-m0-p124-v3091.quick_english: May the great goddess in seed form always protect me on the mountain.

mukta-m0-p124-v3092.quick_english: Protect, protect! hūṃ hūṃ oṃ hrīṃ svāhā, O Maheśvarī.

mukta-m0-p124-v3093.quick_english: oṃ hrīṃ, O Vajrapuṣpe, hūṃ phaṭ, giver of all desires in the border region.

mukta-m0-p124-v3094.quick_english: hūṃ svāhā — may the one united with power always protect my wife.

mukta-m0-p124-v3095.quick_english: oṃ hrīṃ — may the goddess who removes all obstacles always protect me from obstacles.

mukta-m0-p124-v3096.quick_english: May the goddess who destroys all obstacles protect me on the earth.

mukta-m0-p124-v3097.quick_english: May the goddess known by the name Lākinī protect me in the netherworld.

mukta-m0-p124-v3098.quick_english: May the syllable strīṃ, the bride-form goddess-lord Maheśvarī, protect me.

mukta-m0-p124-v3099.quick_english: May Mahāmāyā, whose form is phaṭ, always protect me in the north.

mukta-m0-p124-v3100.quick_english: May Deveśī, the mountain-daughter whose essential nature is hūṃ, protect me in the middle.

mukta-m0-p125-v3101.quick_english: May Bhavani, the bestower of all sovereignty, protect in the house.

mukta-m0-p125-v3102.quick_english: In scripture, in debate, in battle, in water, on difficult ground, and on the mountain.

mukta-m0-p125-v3103.quick_english: In the terrible abode of ghosts and spirits, may the fearsome Durga protect me.

mukta-m0-p125-v3104.quick_english: And I cannot describe the greatness of this armor even in a hundred years.

mukta-m0-p125-v3105.quick_english: Among sons and wives, among relatives, in all places, and always.

mukta-m0-p125-v3106.quick_english: Whether one has become pure or even impure, this armor grants all desires.

mukta-m0-p125-v3107.quick_english: O Great Goddess, one certainly becomes a king among poets in all scriptures.

mukta-m0-p125-v3108.quick_english: In battle, in gambling, and in dispute, victory there will certainly be his.

mukta-m0-p125-v3109.quick_english: Enemies become servants, and he is always beloved of all.

mukta-m0-p125-v3110.quick_english: Even death comes under his control, and the kings of the earth become his servants.

mukta-m0-p125-v3111.quick_english: A mortal who recites or remembers it becomes capable of cursing and blessing.

mukta-m0-p125-v3112.quick_english: The mortal becomes lord of all speech, able to influence the world, and always happy.

mukta-m0-p125-v3113.quick_english: Moreover, O Goddess, this armor is rare in the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p125-v3114.quick_english: But for one who worships without difference, success is not far away.

mukta-m0-p125-v3115.quick_english: One should meditate on light in the navel, likewise in the face, and above the heart.

mukta-m0-p125-v3116.quick_english: O Great Goddess, he should always practice union with a woman.

mukta-m0-p125-v3117.quick_english: A mortal endowed with śakti becomes accomplished; not otherwise.

mukta-m0-p125-v3118.quick_english: O Goddess, having seen that practitioner, they become filled with modesty.

mukta-m0-p125-v3119.quick_english: O Goddess, having seen that best of practitioners, they always praise him.

mukta-m0-p125-v3120.quick_english: All always praise that best of practitioners upon seeing him.

mukta-m0-p125-v3121.quick_english: It directly grants enjoyment and liberation, having the very form of a wish-fulfilling tree.

mukta-m0-p125-v3122.quick_english: O Goddess, for him calamities and troubles from kings quickly perish.

mukta-m0-p125-v3123.quick_english: In his house stable Lakshmi dwells, and in his mouth speech certainly dwells.

mukta-m0-p125-v3124.quick_english: He certainly does not become short-lived, poor, or foolish; there is no doubt.

mukta-m0-p125-v3125.quick_english: For him there may be accomplishment of all aims, whatever exists in his mind.

mukta-m0-p127-v3151.quick_english: May Tārā, composed of thirty-four syllables, protect the entire body.

mukta-m0-p127-v3152.quick_english: And may the ten-syllabled root mantra, beginning and ending with kūrca, protect the upper part.

mukta-m0-p127-v3153.quick_english: By receiving this according to rule, one may lead death onto the path of death.

mukta-m0-p127-v3154.quick_english: Now, O beloved, this has been told to you as a limb of the armor.

mukta-m0-p127-v3155.quick_english: The armor named Trailokyamohana, embodied as mantra.

mukta-m0-p127-v3156.quick_english: Whether thrice or once, according to knowledge, one may become Bhairava in that very moment.

mukta-m0-p127-v3157.quick_english: One may become a guru in all sciences and also qualified in recitation and other practices.

mukta-m0-p127-v3158.quick_english: The hero may wander through the three worlds as a lord of troops, like Guha.

mukta-m0-p127-v3159.quick_english: One may obtain the fruit of worship performed for five thousand years.

mukta-m0-p127-v3160.quick_english: Having become lord of all powers, one may wander like Bhairava.

mukta-m0-p127-v3161.quick_english: In his house, Lakṣmī and Vāṇī will certainly dwell for a long time.

mukta-m0-p127-v3162.quick_english: He does not become short-lived, poor, or foolish; there is indeed no doubt.

mukta-m0-p88-v2179.quick_english: The meaning is: from the middle up to the middle limit.

mukta-m0-p88-v2180.quick_english: Thus the knowing one should make a second hole upon the rim.

mukta-m0-p88-v2181.quick_english: On the outside, one should arrange eight petals by means of two parts.

mukta-m0-p88-v2182.quick_english: This pertains to Purāṇic mantras ending with 'namaḥ'.

mukta-m0-p88-v2183.quick_english: But not 'oṃ ādityāya namaḥ'; this is the water offering, as in 'sūryāya namaḥ' and so forth.

mukta-m0-p88-v2184.quick_english: Therefore, in a mantra ending with 'svāhā', an additional 'svāhā' should not be said.

mukta-m0-p88-v2185.quick_english: Leaving five fingers outside, one should hold it with the śaṅkha mudrā.

mukta-m0-p88-v2186.quick_english: But when the oblation substance is unspecified, sesame and ghee are called the oblation.

mukta-m0-p88-v2187.quick_english: By the fire rite one obtains prosperity and all success.

mukta-m0-p88-v2188.quick_english: The brāhmaṇa should indeed perform the offering to the vaiśya and so forth.

mukta-m0-p88-v2189.quick_english: Having offered, praised, and bowed, one should dismiss in the moon circle.

mukta-m0-p88-v2190.quick_english: Then one should perform the oblation in order beginning with the east.

mukta-m0-p88-v2191.quick_english: In a pit or on a ground altar, consecrated by gazing and so forth.

mukta-m0-p88-v2192.quick_english: By that very means sprinkling is declared; sprinkling with the armor mantra is considered proper.

mukta-m0-p88-v2193.quick_english: Facing north, one should worship Brahmā, Vaivasvata, and the moons.

mukta-m0-p88-v2194.quick_english: Thus one should worship in order.

mukta-m0-p88-v2195.quick_english: Then one should perform the oblation in the presence of the deity.

mukta-m0-p88-v2196.quick_english: One should offer handfuls of flowers; but in the case of Sundarī, with Bālā.

mukta-m0-p88-v2198.quick_english: But in the case of Sundarī, one should worship Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī.

mukta-m0-p88-v2199.quick_english: One should take what is born in the house of Vedic scholars, or what dwells in the forest, or else.

mukta-m0-p88-v2200.quick_english: Therefore, one should bring what has been released from the fire with every effort.

mukta-m0-p94-v2326.quick_english: May klīṃ and the goddess Tripuṭeśānī, giver of sovereignty over the three cities, protect my two hands.

mukta-m0-p94-v2327.quick_english: May krauṃ and the three-syllabled goddess Bhuvaneśvarī protect my navel region.

mukta-m0-p94-v2328.quick_english: May hrīṃ protect my secret region and, with salutation to Bhagavatī, protect my hip.

mukta-m0-p94-v2329.quick_english: May Annapūrṇā always protect, and may svāhā protect my two feet.

mukta-m0-p94-v2330.quick_english: The sixteen-syllabled mantra begins with oṃ, māyā, ramā, and kāma, and continues after that.

mukta-m0-p94-v2331.quick_english: The formula 'oṃ, Durgā, Durgā, protectress, svāhā' is a ten-syllabled mantra.

mukta-m0-p94-v2332.quick_english: This mantra, beginning with the māyā seed, is ten-syllabled, and after it comes another.

mukta-m0-p94-v2333.quick_english: Another mantra, eight-syllabled in nature, is: oṃ, hrīṃ, duṃ, salutation to Durgā.

mukta-m0-p94-v2334.quick_english: Another mantra, eight-syllabled, is: O slayer of Mahiṣa, svāhā.

mukta-m0-p94-v2335.quick_english: The mantra 'māyā, Padmāvatī, svāhā' is declared to be seven-syllabled.

mukta-m0-p94-v2336.quick_english: Enclosed by noose and goad: māyā, come, O supreme goddess, svāhā.

mukta-m0-p94-v2337.quick_english: O Sarasvatī, five-voweled one, ever-moist, flowing with the juice of passion.

mukta-m0-p94-v2338.quick_english: May the armor of oṃ and māyā always protect in the sky, O lady.

mukta-m0-p94-v2339.quick_english: May the eight serpents of Tvaritā always protect me in the Śiva corner.

mukta-m0-p94-v2340.quick_english: May Bhairavī with bindu and Bālā always protect me on the earth.

mukta-m0-p94-v2341.quick_english: It is the most essential of essences, meritorious, the embodiment of a multitude of great vidyās.

mukta-m0-p94-v2342.quick_english: Having given the eightfold flower offering, one should recite once with the root mantra alone.

mukta-m0-p94-v2343.quick_english: Having created mutual affection, Kamalā remains steadfast in the house.

mukta-m0-p94-v2344.quick_english: The virtuous-souled person who wears this, named the auspiciousness of the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p94-v2345.quick_english: Having become endowed with all sovereignty, he becomes a conqueror of the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p94-v2346.quick_english: She may become the mother of many sons, and even a barren woman obtains a son.

mukta-m0-p94-v2347.quick_english: Whoever worships Bhuvaneśvarī without knowing this armor.

mukta-m0-p94-v2348.quick_english: Having obtained supreme poverty, he soon meets death.

mukta-m0-p94-v2349.quick_english: Salutation to you, O goddess Annapūrṇā, dear to devotion; salutation be to you.

mukta-m0-p94-v2350.quick_english: Salutation to you, O Māheśvarī; salutation be to you, O Annapūrṇā.

mukta-m0-p98-v2426.quick_english: She is clad in silk garments and delights with soft anklets.

mukta-m0-p98-v2427.quick_english: She is Vanadurgā and Mataṅgī, worshipped by the sage Mataṅga.

mukta-m0-p98-v2428.quick_english: She is indeed Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, Lakṣmī, and also takes a male form.

mukta-m0-p98-v2429.quick_english: She is Bahulā, full of abundant love, and the rider of all vehicles.

mukta-m0-p98-v2430.quick_english: She is the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha and the destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.

mukta-m0-p98-v2431.quick_english: She consists of all scriptures, is knowledge itself, and likewise bears all weapons.

mukta-m0-p98-v2432.quick_english: She is a maiden, a unique girl, an adolescent, a young woman, and an ascetic.

mukta-m0-p98-v2433.quick_english: She is the great goddess with loosened hair, of terrible form, and bestower of great fruit.

mukta-m0-p98-v2434.quick_english: She is a flame of fire, fierce-faced, Kālarātri, and an ascetic.

mukta-m0-p98-v2435.quick_english: She is Nārāyaṇī, Bhadrakālī, Viṣṇumāyā, and Jalodarī.

mukta-m0-p98-v2436.quick_english: She is Kātyāyanī and Sāvitrī, directly perceptible and a speaker of Brahman.

mukta-m0-p98-v2437.quick_english: O Goddess Pārvatī, nothing is unattainable for you in the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p98-v2438.quick_english: One may obtain the fourfold aim of life and, in the end, eternal liberation.

mukta-m0-p98-v2439.quick_english: One should worship with supreme devotion while reciting the hundred and eight names.

mukta-m0-p98-v2440.quick_english: Kings become servants, and one may obtain royal prosperity.

mukta-m0-p98-v2441.quick_english: Having drawn the yantra according to rule, the knower of rules may be so; the enemy of Pura always wears it.

mukta-m0-p98-v2442.quick_english: Having drawn it and reciting the hymn, he becomes a giver of prosperity.

mukta-m0-p98-v2443.quick_english: Having recited and worn it, a person may be freed from danger.

mukta-m0-p98-v2444.quick_english: He does not obtain its fruit and may go to hell because of others.

mukta-m0-p98-v2445.quick_english: It must be concealed with effort; be attentive and keep this in mind.

mukta-m0-p98-v2446.quick_english: May Khecarī protect the eyes, and may Catvaravāsinī protect the ears.

mukta-m0-p98-v2447.quick_english: May Caṇḍikā protect the tongue, and likewise may Saubhadrikā protect the neck.

mukta-m0-p98-v2448.quick_english: May Mahāvāṇī protect the throat, and may the world-mother protect the two breasts.

mukta-m0-p98-v2449.quick_english: May the venerable goddess protect the hips, and may Vindhyavāsinī protect the two thighs.

mukta-m0-p98-v2450.quick_english: Protect me in all my limbs, O Durgā, O goddess; homage be to you.

mukta-m0-p99-v2451.quick_english: Whoever rises in the morning and recites this obtains the fruit of all holy places.

mukta-m0-p99-v2452.quick_english: For one who is afraid, there is no fear from ghosts, spirits, or demons.

mukta-m0-p99-v2453.quick_english: He obtains worship everywhere on earth, like a son of the goddess.

mukta-m0-p99-v2454.quick_english: May my mind-swan rejoice for a long time in the attained endless ocean of essence.

mukta-m0-p99-v2455.quick_english: O enemy of elephants, what fear from enemies is there for those who serve you?

mukta-m0-p99-v2456.quick_english: Honor me today, who am devoted to that kiss.

mukta-m0-p99-v2457.quick_english: May our minds always be engaged in the contemplation of the venerable lotus feet.

mukta-m0-p99-v2458.quick_english: O bestower of welfare, may unbroken prosperity spread in my mind, and may I be forgiven.

mukta-m0-p99-v2460.quick_english: May the flood of the essence of venerable devotion, like an excessively rainy day, always flow.

mukta-m0-p99-v2461.quick_english: May that splendor, like blossomed collyrium and a blue cloud, always be in our minds.

mukta-m0-p99-v2462.quick_english: May she who delights in victory and is skilled in tearing apart the enemies of the visible deities be victorious.

mukta-m0-p99-v2463.quick_english: In that blazing place where all birds are broken and shattered, tormented by hunger and thirst.

mukta-m0-p99-v2464.quick_english: One should remember her whirling with the joy of battle in the beautiful courtyard.

mukta-m0-p99-v2465.quick_english: Remember her with a terrible, shining face striking down stumbling heroes, vehement with fierce, loud laughter.

mukta-m0-p99-v2467.quick_english: The worlds come into one's hand; O Mother, salutation to you, victory!

mukta-m0-p99-v2468.quick_english: Having obtained whose grace, one may become Sadāśiva himself.

mukta-m0-p99-v2469.quick_english: One should recite this armor daily for the accomplishment of the mantra syllables.

mukta-m0-p99-v2470.quick_english: The primordial power is the deity; the application is for the attainment of the fruits of the four goals of life.

mukta-m0-p99-v2471.quick_english: May the syllable ma and the goddess Maheśvarī protect me in the pair of eyes.

mukta-m0-p99-v2472.quick_english: May the syllable ṣa and the white, invincible goddess protect me on the tongue.

mukta-m0-p99-v2473.quick_english: May the syllable ṛ and the goddess Sāvitrī, the destroyer of time, protect me.

mukta-m0-p99-v2474.quick_english: Likewise on the crown, in the armor, on the foot, on the face, and on the pair of calves.

mukta-m0-p99-v2475.quick_english: May Kāmā and the others, Svāhā the crusher, protect me—my head and all my limbs.

mukta-m0-p100-v2477.plain_english: May the Crusher protect always; may the Crusher guard forever.
mukta-m0-p100-v2477.sanskrit_cite: marddinī pātu satataṃ marddinī rakṣayet sadā

mukta-m0-p100-v2478.plain_english: May the Radiant One protect, O Great Goddess; may the Golden One guard always.

mukta-m0-p100-v2479.plain_english: May the Radiant One protect; may Great Illusion and Illusion always protect me.
mukta-m0-p100-v2479.sanskrit_cite: prabhā pātu mahāmāyā māyā pātu sadā mam

mukta-m0-p100-v2480.plain_english: May the Delightful One protect always; may the Very Radiant One guard at all times.

mukta-m0-p100-v2481.plain_english: May the powers protect always; may they always protect my seal.
mukta-m0-p100-v2481.sanskrit_cite: śaktayaḥ pāntu satataṃ mudrāṃ pāntu sadā mam

mukta-m0-p100-v2482.plain_english: May the yoginīs protect always; may the sky-movers guard at all times.
mukta-m0-p100-v2482.sanskrit_cite: yoginyaḥ pāntu satataṃ khecaryaḥ pāntu sarvadā

mukta-m0-p100-v2483.plain_english: May the goddess, the Crusher of the Buffalo, protect everywhere and always.

mukta-m0-p100-v2484.plain_english: Wherever one is, it must not be spoken; it must be carefully concealed.
mukta-m0-p100-v2484.sanskrit_cite: yatra tatra na vaktavyaṃ gopitavyaṃ prayatnataḥ

mukta-m0-p100-v2485.plain_english: Knowledge is easily found everywhere, but this great armor is hard to obtain.
mukta-m0-p100-v2485.sanskrit_cite: sarvatra sulabhā vidyā kavacaṃ durlabhaṃ mahat

mukta-m0-p100-v2486.plain_english: One should not show the divine hymn or the armor, which is hard for even the gods to obtain.

mukta-m0-p100-v2487.plain_english: O Great Goddess, if it is given to them, one's powers perish gradually.
mukta-m0-p100-v2487.sanskrit_cite: dattvā tebhyo maheśāni naśyanti siddhayaḥ kramāt

mukta-m0-p100-v2488.plain_english: And inauspiciousness may come to him; therefore one should conceal it with effort.

mukta-m0-p100-v2489.plain_english: Having written it during an auspicious conjunction, and likewise in Brahma-Indra and in Vaidhṛti...
mukta-m0-p100-v2489.sanskrit_cite: likhitvā śubhayoge ca brahmendre vaidhṛtau tathā

mukta-m0-p100-v2490.plain_english: In Vaṇija, in Śravaṇā, and in Revatī or in Punarvasu...

mukta-m0-p100-v2491.plain_english: In Aśvinī or in Rohiṇī, or on the third or ninth lunar day...

mukta-m0-p100-v2492.plain_english: On the new moon or on the full moon, at night, and likewise in a secluded place...
mukta-m0-p100-v2492.sanskrit_cite: kuhvāṃ vā pūrṇimāyāṃ vā niśāyāṃ prāntare tathā

mukta-m0-p100-v2493.plain_english: By a guru or by Vaiṣṇavas, and likewise with self-born flowers...

mukta-m0-p100-v2494.plain_english: Then one should wear the armor, a great protection that grants all desires.

mukta-m0-p100-v2495.plain_english: Seeing him, an opponent becomes mute, and a king becomes like a servant.
mukta-m0-p100-v2495.sanskrit_cite: vādī mūko bhaveddṛṣṭvā rājā ca sevakāyate

mukta-m0-p100-v2496.plain_english: In six months or in three months, one certainly becomes a sky-mover.

mukta-m0-p100-v2497.plain_english: One becomes disease-free and strong, and even a king may become a servant.

mukta-m0-p100-v2498.plain_english: The wise one who acts thus is indeed the auspicious Sadāśiva.
mukta-m0-p100-v2498.sanskrit_cite: ya evaṃ kurute dhīmān sa eva śrīsadāśivaḥ

mukta-m0-p100-v2499.plain_english: As you are immovable, O Kṛṣṇā, so be steady in me.
mukta-m0-p100-v2499.sanskrit_cite: yathā tvamacalā kṛṣṇe tathā bhava mayi sthirā

mukta-m0-p100-v2500.plain_english: Padmā, the lotus-abiding goddess, is prosperity itself, supremely exalted and holding the auspicious lotus.

mukta-m0-p101-v2501.plain_english: May steady fortune be his, together with his son, wife, and others.

mukta-m0-p101-v2502.plain_english: By whose mere knowledge one may become Sadāśiva himself.

mukta-m0-p101-v2503.plain_english: He may become the son of Pārvatī, honored by all the scriptures.

mukta-m0-p101-v2504.plain_english: Kamalā, beloved of Viṣṇu, should always be served by those who seek knowledge.

mukta-m0-p101-v2505.plain_english: May hrīṃ and Śāṅkarī protect the space between the eyes and the pair of eyes.
mukta-m0-p101-v2505.sanskrit_cite: hrīṃ pātu cakṣuṣormadhye cakṣuryugme ca śāṅkarī

mukta-m0-p101-v2506.plain_english: At the base of the lips, in the row of teeth, at the root of the palate, and again in the jaw.

mukta-m0-p101-v2507.plain_english: In the region of the back, likewise in the secret part, and on the left and right sides as well.
mukta-m0-p101-v2507.sanskrit_cite: pṛṣṭhadeśe tathā guhye vāme ca dakṣiṇe tathā

mukta-m0-p101-v2508.plain_english: In the knee circle, in the pair of feet, and at the base of the ankles and toes.

mukta-m0-p101-v2509.plain_english: May Kāmeśī, the exalted great goddess, protect every limb.

mukta-m0-p101-v2510.plain_english: May the seer protect; O goddess, beloved of Śambhu, may you always protect everywhere.
mukta-m0-p101-v2510.sanskrit_cite: ṛṣiḥ pātu sadā devi sarvatra śambhuvallabhā

mukta-m0-p101-v2511.plain_english: May Ramā, the great goddess, protect; may Māyā, self-ruling by herself, protect.
mukta-m0-p101-v2511.sanskrit_cite: ramā pātu mahādevī pātu māyā svarāṭ svayam

mukta-m0-p101-v2512.plain_english: May Vijayā protect in the house; may Jayā always protect me.
mukta-m0-p101-v2512.sanskrit_cite: vijayā pātu bhavane jayā pātu sadā mama

mukta-m0-p101-v2513.plain_english: May Bhairavī protect everywhere; may Bheruṇḍā always protect.

mukta-m0-p101-v2514.plain_english: May Kālikā always protect me; may Kālarātri always protect.
mukta-m0-p101-v2514.sanskrit_cite: pātu māṃ kālikā nityaṃ kālarātriḥ sadā'vatu

mukta-m0-p101-v2515.plain_english: May the Yoginīs always protect; may the Mudrās always protect me.
mukta-m0-p101-v2515.sanskrit_cite: yoginyaḥ sarvadā pāntu mudrāḥ pāntu sadā mama

mukta-m0-p101-v2516.plain_english: Everywhere, in all tasks, in all actions, and always.

mukta-m0-p101-v2517.plain_english: Thus this divine armor has been told to you for the accomplishment of all powers.
mukta-m0-p101-v2517.sanskrit_cite: iti te kathitaṃ divyaṃ kavacaṃ sarvasiddhaye

mukta-m0-p101-v2518.plain_english: O great goddess, not to the deceitful, not to one devoid of devotion, and not to a slanderer.

mukta-m0-p101-v2519.plain_english: One should not show this divine hymn; from showing it, there may be loss of Śiva's grace.

mukta-m0-p101-v2520.plain_english: One should give this supreme armor to a pure Vaiṣṇava.

mukta-m0-p101-v2521.plain_english: One should give the armor; thus it is said, in agreement with all the tantras.

mukta-m0-p101-v2522.plain_english: One should write the mantra with lac, endowed with all the circles.

mukta-m0-p101-v2523.plain_english: With one's own fluids and others' fluids, and endowed with various fragrances.

mukta-m0-p101-v2524.plain_english: On a good lunar day, on an auspicious conjunction, or in Śravaṇā on a Sunday.

mukta-m0-p101-v2525.plain_english: Or when Pūrvabhādrapadā is in conjunction, or in Svātī, on a Tuesday.

mukta-m0-p105-v2601.plain_english: I worship Rama every day, together with Sita and Lakshmana.

mukta-m0-p105-v2602.plain_english: For him the directions are filled with Shiva, and the powers become his maidservants.

mukta-m0-p105-v2603.plain_english: Whoever recites this daily will become devoted to Rama.
mukta-m0-p105-v2603.sanskrit_cite: paṭhedanudinaṃ yastu sa rāme bhaktimān bhavet

mukta-m0-p105-v2604.plain_english: There is no higher secret than this in the three worlds.
mukta-m0-p105-v2604.sanskrit_cite: nātaḥ parataraṃ guhyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu vidyate

mukta-m0-p105-v2605.plain_english: Then, seated to eat, Shankara spoke to Parvati.

mukta-m0-p105-v2606.plain_english: Then I shall eat, O god; let it be eaten by you, O lord.
mukta-m0-p105-v2606.sanskrit_cite: tato bhokṣyāmyahaṃ deva bhujyatāṃ bhavatā prabho

mukta-m0-p105-v2607.plain_english: You are blessed, you are meritorious, and you are a devotee of Vishnu, O Parvati.

mukta-m0-p105-v2608.plain_english: O Parvati, as I hear the names beginning with the syllable ra.

mukta-m0-p105-v2609.plain_english: Thus, by the word Rama, the supreme Brahman is designated.

mukta-m0-p105-v2610.plain_english: Having said 'Rama,' O great goddess, eat together with me now.

mukta-m0-p105-v2611.plain_english: Then, having eaten, the great goddess remained together with her husband.
mukta-m0-p105-v2611.sanskrit_cite: tato bhuktvā mahādevī patinā saha saṃsthitā

mukta-m0-p105-v2612.plain_english: Let it be told to me, O lord; in that I have supreme delight.
mukta-m0-p105-v2612.sanskrit_cite: kathyatāṃ mama deveśa tatra me prītiruttamā

mukta-m0-p105-v2613.plain_english: The names of auspicious Rama are more than a thousand.

mukta-m0-p105-v2614.plain_english: Each single name of Vishnu bears fruit surpassing all the Vedas.

mukta-m0-p105-v2615.plain_english: Therefore, merit multiplied a crore times is obtained by the name of Rama alone.

mukta-m0-p105-v2616.plain_english: Lotus-eyed, glorious, lord of kings, chief of the Raghu dynasty.

mukta-m0-p105-v2617.plain_english: Dear to Vishvamitra, self-controlled, devoted to protecting those who seek refuge.

mukta-m0-p105-v2618.plain_english: Vowed to truth, the fruit of vows, always the shelter of Hanuman.

mukta-m0-p105-v2619.plain_english: Protector of Vibhishana, remover of the heads of the ten-necked one.

mukta-m0-p105-v2620.plain_english: The fire to the great pride of Parashurama, the slayer of Tadaka.

mukta-m0-p105-v2621.plain_english: Slayer of Dushana and Trishiras, three-formed, the three qualities, and the three Vedas.

mukta-m0-p105-v2622.plain_english: Protector of the three worlds, bowman, maker of merit in the Dandaka forest.

mukta-m0-p105-v2623.plain_english: Protector in the matter of Jayanta, giver of boons, served by the son of Sumitra.

mukta-m0-p105-v2624.plain_english: Slayer of the illusory Maricha, possessed of great lordship, and mighty-armed.

mukta-m0-p105-v2625.plain_english: He is a great yogi and greatly noble, the giver of the desired kingdom to Sugrīva.

mukta-m0-p109-v2701.plain_english: It is visualized as a dense, cloud-like mass, like the essence of pearls, released in both broken and unbroken streams.

mukta-m0-p109-v2702.plain_english: He is constantly beheld by herds of cows along with their calves looking up.

mukta-m0-p109-v2703.plain_english: He is adorned by cowherds with sticks and nooses raised in their hands.

mukta-m0-p109-v2704.plain_english: The supreme of the supreme is praised with speech that is affectionate and very tender.

mukta-m0-p109-v2705.plain_english: Satisfied with him at the three daily junctures, he grants the desired boon.

mukta-m0-p109-v2706.plain_english: He certainly obtains unshakable prosperity and becomes eloquent.
mukta-m0-p109-v2706.sanskrit_cite: acalāṃ śriyamāpnoti sa vāgmī jāyate dhruvam

mukta-m0-p109-v2707.plain_english: O lord, out of compassion please tell the teaching named Trailokyamaṅgala, auspicious for the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p109-v2708.plain_english: It was formerly told out of compassion by Nārāyaṇa to Brahmā.

mukta-m0-p109-v2709.plain_english: It is the most secret truth, embodied as a multitude of Brahman-mantras.

mukta-m0-p109-v2710.plain_english: Having held it and through its recitation, Mahālakṣmī protects the three worlds.

mukta-m0-p109-v2711.plain_english: Durgā, the mother of the three worlds, overcomes Mahiṣa and other great demons.

mukta-m0-p109-v2712.plain_english: Thus Indra and all the other gods may obtain complete sovereignty.

mukta-m0-p109-v2713.plain_english: One should reveal it to a disciple who is endowed with devotion and is a practitioner.

mukta-m0-p109-v2714.plain_english: Prajāpati is the seer of this Trailokyamaṅgala armor.

mukta-m0-p109-v2715.plain_english: Its application is declared for dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation.

mukta-m0-p109-v2716.plain_english: May the eight-syllabled mantra, giver of enjoyment and liberation, protect my forehead and pair of eyes.

mukta-m0-p109-v2717.plain_english: May 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya' always protect my nose, and 'govindāya' protect my tongue.
mukta-m0-p109-v2717.sanskrit_cite: klīṃ kṛṣṇāya sadā ghrāṇaṃ govindāyeti jihvikām

mukta-m0-p109-v2718.plain_english: May the eighteen-syllabled great mantra and the ten-syllabled mantra protect my throat.

mukta-m0-p109-v2719.plain_english: O Lady of the worlds, may my heart, my two hands, and my breasts be protected by 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya'.
mukta-m0-p109-v2719.sanskrit_cite: hṛdayaṃ bhuvaneśāni klīṃ kṛṣṇāya karau stanau mama

mukta-m0-p109-v2720.plain_english: May the best of mantras, 'klīṃ kṛṣṇāya', always protect my pair of sides.
mukta-m0-p109-v2720.sanskrit_cite: klīṃ kṛṣṇāya sadā pātu pārśvayugmaṃ manūttamaḥ

mukta-m0-p109-v2721.plain_english: May the eight-syllabled mantra protect my navel, and may the two-syllabled 'kṛṣṇa' protect it.

mukta-m0-p109-v2722.plain_english: May 'śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ' together with the Kṛṣṇa-ṭha pair always protect my thighs.
mukta-m0-p109-v2722.sanskrit_cite: sakthinīṃ satataṃ pātu śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇaṭhadvayam

mukta-m0-p109-v2723.plain_english: Then, after 'śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ', comes the word 'gopījanavallabha'.
mukta-m0-p109-v2723.sanskrit_cite: śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ padato gopījanavallabhapadaṃ tataḥ

mukta-m0-p109-v2724.plain_english: And may 'hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ' and the ten-syllabled mantra always protect my knees.
mukta-m0-p109-v2724.sanskrit_cite: jānunī ca sāda pātu hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ca daśākṣaraḥ

mukta-m0-p109-v2725.plain_english: This mantra is eighteen-syllabled; when preceded by hrīṃ and śrīṃ, it becomes twenty-syllabled.

mukta-m0-p120-v2976.plain_english: It should be given to a devoted disciple who is dearer even than one's own life-breaths.

mukta-m0-p120-v2977.plain_english: The sage is Ṛṣi, the meter is Virāṭ, and the deity is Chinnamastakā.

mukta-m0-p120-v2978.plain_english: May the hūṃ syllable protect my head, and may Chinnamastā, radiant with strength, protect it.
mukta-m0-p120-v2978.sanskrit_cite: hūṃkāro me śiraḥ pātu chinnamastā balaprabhā

mukta-m0-p120-v2979.plain_english: May śrīṃ, hrīṃ, hūṃ, and aiṃ protect my two eyes, and may she who holds three severed heads also protect them.
mukta-m0-p120-v2979.sanskrit_cite: śrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ aiṃ dṛśau pātu muṇḍakatrīdharāpi sā

mukta-m0-p120-v2980.plain_english: The mantra beginning with dhruva is: vajravairocanīye huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
mukta-m0-p120-v2980.sanskrit_cite: vajravairocanīye huṃ phaṭ svāhā ca dhruvādikā

mukta-m0-p120-v2981.plain_english: With the seed syllables śrīṃ, māyā, kūrca, and vāk, followed by vajravairocanīye and hūṃ.

mukta-m0-p120-v2982.plain_english: At her own sides, joyfully causing the stream of blood to be drunk.

mukta-m0-p120-v2983.plain_english: Holding a severed head and scissors, red in color, she grants the desires of the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p120-v2984.plain_english: May the formula beginning with ramā protect the tongue, and may the formula beginning with lajjā protect the throat.
mukta-m0-p120-v2984.sanskrit_cite: ramādyā pātu jihvāṃ ca lajjādyā pātu kaṇṭhakam

mukta-m0-p120-v2985.plain_english: May the mantra enclosed by ramā protect the two sides, and may Sureśvarī protect them.
mukta-m0-p120-v2985.sanskrit_cite: ramayā puṭitā vidyā pāśvauṃ pātu sureśvarī

mukta-m0-p120-v2986.plain_english: May the goddess enclosed by kūrca always protect the back region.

mukta-m0-p120-v2987.plain_english: Īśvarī, with the seed syllables kūrca and vāk, vajravairocanīye, hūṃ.

mukta-m0-p120-v2988.plain_english: May Chinnamastā, together with her śakti, always protect the pair of thighs.

mukta-m0-p120-v2989.plain_english: May the eternal one who abides in all mantras always protect all my limbs.

mukta-m0-p120-v2990.plain_english: May Ḍākinī protect me on the right, and may Śrī Mahābhairavī protect me.
mukta-m0-p120-v2990.sanskrit_cite: ḍākinī dakṣiṇe pātu śrīmahābhairavī ca mām

mukta-m0-p120-v2991.plain_english: May Indrākṣī protect in the northwest, and may Asitāṅgī protect in the north.

mukta-m0-p120-v2992.plain_english: Thus may these eight śaktis, bearing scissors, protect in the directions and intermediate directions.

mukta-m0-p120-v2993.plain_english: Hrīṃ, hrīṃ, may she protect me on the right; O Kālikā on the right, may you protect me.
mukta-m0-p120-v2993.sanskrit_cite: hrīṃ hrīṃ māṃ dakṣiṇe pātu dakṣiṇe kālike'vatu

mukta-m0-p120-v2994.plain_english: Hūṃ, hūṃ, may she protect in the northwest; svāhā, may she always protect in the north.
mukta-m0-p120-v2994.sanskrit_cite: hūṃ hūṃ pātu marutkoṇe svāhā pātu sadottare

mukta-m0-p120-v2995.plain_english: Tāra, māyā, vadhū, kūrca, and the phaṭ syllable—this is the great mantra.
mukta-m0-p120-v2995.sanskrit_cite: tāro māyā vadhūḥ kūrcaṃ phaṭkāro'yaṃ mahāmanuḥ

mukta-m0-p120-v2996.plain_english: Tārā, accompanied in the sky, is then Mahānīla Sarasvatī.

mukta-m0-p120-v2997.plain_english: By holding and reciting this, one is remembered as the terrible Bhairava named Krodha.

mukta-m0-p120-v2998.plain_english: By whose command Madhumatī goes to the vicinity of the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p120-v2999.plain_english: By the grace of that armor, they receive his command.

mukta-m0-p120-v3000.plain_english: Having worshipped the goddess with fragrance and other offerings, one should recite once using only the root-mantra.

mukta-m0-p124-v3076.plain_english: May the syllable hūṃ, bearing the form of Bhavānī's power, protect me in the heart.

mukta-m0-p124-v3077.plain_english: May Kharvā, the fear-removing goddess-lord, protect me on both cheeks.

mukta-m0-p124-v3078.plain_english: May the goddess covered with a tiger skin, beloved of Śiva, protect me on the hip.

mukta-m0-p124-v3079.plain_english: And may the goddess with red, round eyes always protect me in the hip region.

mukta-m0-p124-v3080.plain_english: May the terrible-mouthed goddess, beloved of Hara, always protect me on the generative organ.
mukta-m0-p124-v3080.sanskrit_cite: karālāsyā sadā pātu liṅge devī harapriyā

mukta-m0-p124-v3081.plain_english: May the great goddess Maheśvarī, holding a corpse-skull, protect me on the knee-wheel.

mukta-m0-p124-v3082.plain_english: Then may the goddess wearing snake earrings protect me on both feet.

mukta-m0-p124-v3083.plain_english: May the goddess wearing snake-bone ornaments protect me in the border region.

mukta-m0-p124-v3084.plain_english: May the great goddess holding a sword always protect me in the ear.

mukta-m0-p124-v3085.plain_english: May the goddess holding scissors always protect me in disputes among enemies.

mukta-m0-p124-v3086.plain_english: May the goddess wearing snake bracelets always protect me while eating.

mukta-m0-p124-v3087.plain_english: May the goddess seated in the hero posture always protect me during sleep.

mukta-m0-p124-v3088.plain_english: May the goddess whose hip is girdled with a snake protect me in all actions.

mukta-m0-p124-v3089.plain_english: May the goddess situated in the middle of a pyre always protect me in acts of killing.

mukta-m0-p124-v3090.plain_english: May the ornamented goddess, beloved of Hara, protect me.

mukta-m0-p124-v3091.plain_english: May the great goddess in seed form always protect me on the mountain.

mukta-m0-p52-v1296.plain_english: And because of the fruitlessness of the bindu, she bestows the fruit of liberation.

mukta-m0-p56-v1389.plain_english: One should arrange the offering just as before.

mukta-m0-p56-v1391.plain_english: The Bhadrakālī mantra grants the four aims of life and brings auspiciousness.

mukta-m0-p56-v1392.plain_english: The Śmaśānakālikā mantra is considered to have twenty-one syllables.

mukta-m0-p56-v1400.plain_english: Because she rescues from fierce calamities, she is proclaimed as Ugratārā.

mukta-m0-p58-v1426.plain_english: Having uttered the all-speech-form, one should remember it for the weapon with the syllable phaṭ.

mukta-m0-p58-v1428.plain_english: It always grants all desires and bestows universal sovereignty.

mukta-m0-p58-v1429.plain_english: To one who is generous, noble-born, and devoted to pure conduct.

mukta-m0-p58-v1430.plain_english: O Goddess, having performed it thus, one should reveal it to the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p58-v1431.plain_english: Otherwise there would be loss of success; thus is the command made by the Śaṅkaras.

mukta-m0-p58-v1432.plain_english: The Rudras, accompanied by one, are declared to be fifty.

mukta-m0-p58-v1436.plain_english: Thus ends the installation of the world guardians.

mukta-m0-p58-v1437.plain_english: Then, O Goddess, after the supreme Śiva, six Śivas are declared.

mukta-m0-p58-v1438.plain_english: Everywhere, having uttered the three-syllable mantra, one should use the sequence from va to sa together with bindu.

mukta-m0-p58-v1439.plain_english: Having placed the sequence from va to la in the navel, indeed in the maṇipūraka.

mukta-m0-p58-v1440.plain_english: In the anāhata, one should place the sequence from ka to ṭha, along with Īśvara and Kākinī.

mukta-m0-p58-v1441.plain_english: Then one should place Sadāśiva and Śākinī as before.

mukta-m0-p58-v1442.plain_english: One should place the supreme Śiva, in the form of Brahman, accompanied by Hākinī.

mukta-m0-p58-v1444.plain_english: Thus ends the installation of Tārā and so forth.

mukta-m0-p58-v1445.plain_english: On the hip: 3, obeisance to the Kāñcī seat.

mukta-m0-p58-v1446.plain_english: Akṣobhya, by the grace of this installation, is for all beings.

mukta-m0-p58-v1447.plain_english: O beautiful-hipped one, the sixfold Tārā is declared to be performed in order and in reverse order.

mukta-m0-p58-v1448.plain_english: He becomes worthy of worship by the yoginīs; he is not a god, but indeed a human.

mukta-m0-p58-v1449.plain_english: For him who illuminates the faces of his father and mother, there is none in the worlds worthy of his worship.

mukta-m0-p58-v1450.plain_english: One should place the syllables beginning with ḍa, endowed with bindu and visarga, along the path of maintenance.

mukta-m0-p79-v1951.plain_english: Having done this, one should satisfy the dancer with devotion; then she acts sufficiently.

mukta-m0-p79-v1952.plain_english: Day by day she gives a hundred pieces of gold and substances for accomplishment.

mukta-m0-p79-v1953.plain_english: The practitioner knows all news of the past and the future.

mukta-m0-p79-v1954.plain_english: Whatever he desires, she gives all of that; there is no doubt here.

mukta-m0-p79-v1955.plain_english: Having performed the life-installation and so forth, one should meditate there with a clear mind.

mukta-m0-p79-v1956.plain_english: Having meditated thus, one should recite the mantra a thousand times day by day.
mukta-m0-p79-v1956.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ dhyātvā japenmantraṃ sahasrantu dine dine

mukta-m0-p79-v1957.plain_english: One should worship with joy at the three twilights, using offerings of incense and lamp.

mukta-m0-p79-v1959.plain_english: She certainly gives divine chewable foods, suckable items, and other substances.

mukta-m0-p79-v1960.plain_english: Having brought them, they are truly given according to the desire of the practitioner.

mukta-m0-p79-v1962.plain_english: The best of practitioners rejoiced together with the goddess day by day.

mukta-m0-p79-v1963.plain_english: The mantra known as the consort of fire is declared to be the giver of all accomplishments.

mukta-m0-p79-v1964.plain_english: Indeed, this secret of secrets has been proclaimed to you out of affection.

mukta-m0-p83-v2051.plain_english: The knowers of tantra have said that mantra accomplishment is certain.

mukta-m0-p83-v2053.plain_english: Such qualities and the like are the characteristic of middle accomplishment.
